newsitem.title: GERMANY: Nestle Germany will not use gene-altered soy.
newsitem.headline: Nestle Germany will not use gene-altered soy.

text.p: Nestle Deutschland AG, part of the Swiss Nestle group, will not use soy products derived from genetically modified U.S. beans from the 1996/97 harvest, a Nestle spokesman said on Friday.
"We won't use genetically altered soy products from the new U.S. crop," he said.
"We use such small soya volumes that we can switch to other origins or other products," he said.
He estimated annual soy use at 2,000 tonnes in such products as mayonnaise and confectionery at Nestle Deutschland, adding that the decision applied only to the German operations of the Nestle group.
The spokesman said the company was responding to expected consumer opposition, but believed the new products were safe.
"It's got nothing to do with risks, we simply want the consumer to like our products and to avoid irriations over whether they might contain gene soya."
On Thursday, the German unit of Anglo-Dutch group Unilever said it would not sell products containing oils from gene-altered U.S. soybeans.

This followed a campaign by the German branch of environmentalist group Greenpeace, consumer organisations and others against the new beans, which have been genetically modified to resist a weed killer in a technique developed by chemicals company Monsanto.
The campaigners say risks to human health and the environment from the new beans cannot be ruled out.
